description: Local stdio MCP server proxying an allow-listed subset of tools from any hosted MCP server that uses OAuth, refreshing the signed-in person's token as needed.

outputs.description: No asset -- registers a Dagster resource (a stdio MCP server) for other components to reference via server_resource_key.

resource_key.label: Resource Key
resource_key.description: Dagster resource key other components reference via server_resource_key.

oauth_dir.label: Oauth Dir
oauth_dir.description: Directory holding tokens.json + client_info.json from `python -m dagster_community_components.resources.mcp_oauth_login`. Treat as a secret.

allow.label: Allow
allow.description: Tool allow-list -- default EMPTY, so no tools are exposed until you explicitly choose some (unlike notion_mcp_server's 'both tools by default': an arbitrary hosted server's tool surface is unknown ahead of time and may include destructive write/delete tools).

max_requests_per_second.label: Max Requests Per Second
max_requests_per_second.description: Shared by every tool call this server process makes -- see HostedMcpRateLimiter.

max_retries.label: Max Retries
max_retries.description: Retries on a real HTTP 429, a soft text-based rate-limit signal, or a transient error before returning {'error': ...} to the agent.

soft_rate_limit_pattern.label: Soft Rate Limit Pattern
soft_rate_limit_pattern.description: Regex matched against a tool result's TEXT to detect a server that signals rate limits as ordinary text instead of HTTP 429 (Notion's hosted server is the confirmed example -- see notion_mcp_documents). Unset: a generic default pattern ('rate limit', 'too many requests', 'retry...after') is used, which may not match every server's own wording.

token_store.label: Token Store
token_store.description: 'folder' (default): read tokens.json/client_info.json from oauth_dir, refreshing in place when the access token expires -- needs persistent storage with exactly one writer, which is hard to guarantee in a Hybrid/container deployment. 'state': read the current access token from Dagster's own defs_state_storage (state_key) instead -- a SEPARATE, scheduled McpTokenRefresherComponent is the only thing that ever refreshes and writes a new version; this component (and the stdio subprocess it spawns) only ever reads the latest one and never refreshes it itself. If the access token is already expired and the refresher hasn't run recently enough, build_defs raises a clear 'refresh job has not run' error rather than loading with a stale/expired token.

state_key.label: State Key
state_key.description: token_store='state' only (required then). The defs_state_storage key this server's token is stored under -- must match the --state-key used at sign-in (`mcp_oauth_login --state-key ...`) and McpTokenRefresherComponent's own state_key.

instructions.label: Instructions
instructions.description: Free-text usage guidance for this server -- read by the litellm/openai/anthropic/gemini agent components and appended to their system prompt under a heading with this resource's name, so every agent referencing it via server_resource_key gets the same guidance with no copy-paste.
